metadata.setup_attempt: A missing compiler dependency caused an incomplete prior attempt; its complete structured records are retained separately. Fresh complete matrix after setup correction; unrolled 64-step stress probes have a predeclared 30-second outer bound.
metadata.scope: initial synthetic CPU baseline; no accelerator change or speedup claim

hardware.thread_policy: singleton inherited CPU affinity; one requested BLAS/OpenMP thread

limitations: Public synthetic fixtures only; no application-level performance claim.
Singleton logical-CPU affinity limits execution; actual library thread-pool sizes are not individually sampled inside existing workers.
Replay probe has one execution per worker; repeated process results are not warm medians.
Compiler selected JIT compilation follows qualification/backend initialization; not whole-process cold JAX startup.
SSA drift/invariant checks supplement existing distribution/replay tests; not a new stochastic-law qualification.
No CPU CI/check workload runs concurrently with this baseline.
Full simulation-to-observation timing, float32 sweeps and GPU/device-transfer measurements remain follow-up coverage.
additional_limitations: The initial SSA harness has setup/execution/event/storage fields but no per-worker peak-RSS observation.
Source working trees include only documentation edits relative to the recorded numerical revisions.
The incomplete setup attempt and its 32 records are retained separately and excluded from the corrected complete matrix aggregates.
Compiler/SSA setup was repaired by installing declared compiler dependencies; NumPy/JAX/Torch/Diffrax versions were unchanged.
The first incomplete attempt used a 180-second bound for large unrolled probes; the complete restarted matrix declared a 30-second bound. Those censored rows are not combined as measurements.

Compiler normalization/compile_rhs repeat within each process and may reuse caches. Raw samples preserve the initial call; use first samples for cold-process generation costs rather than labeling the within-process median cold.
